author: codex:/root
conclusion: The revised document correctly separates source capabilities, actual current evidence and proposed behavior. Its phased direction is reasonable for discussion: retain the existing Go/SQLite/Mu authority, unify host connection and public product entry points, then add bounded recoverable iteration and delivery acceptance. No implementation authorization or product acceptance is issued by this review.

resolved_document_findings.issue: The original statement that planning compilation only supports json_report omitted an existing dedicated Monitor branch.
resolved_document_findings.resolution: The revised table explicitly restricts ordinary planning nodes to json_report/fixed JSON comparison and acknowledges the dedicated monitor loop. This matches planningNodeSupported and planningOrder.

resolved_document_findings.issue: The original default-path wording could imply that changing CLI cwd itself creates a second database.
resolved_document_findings.resolution: The revised text says a different CLI cwd first fails discovery; database islands require separate Core/bundle data roots. The CLI entry does not create another SQLite/Core.

verified_facts.finding: The proposal records 54 fixture-render checks, 12 independently run Node tests and the source-bound development build/dry-run. It explicitly does not claim a current real Core/provider closed loop or installation.

verified_facts.topic: Shared core and split default discovery
verified_facts.finding: The ordinary CLI/Desktop session path reaches the shared v2 transaction/journal. CLI discovery/config defaults are cwd-relative; Desktop defaults resolve against its repository-shaped app root. The distribution shim only delegates to its own executable. The revised proposal states this accurately.

DesktopManagement rejects an existing live Core as EXTERNAL_HOST_PRESENT, while boot separately continues ordinary health/v2 connection. The proposal preserves the guard and calls for explicit OWNED versus ATTACHED semantics rather than deleting identity protection.
createFiniteGoal creates one mu_turn Task with wall_time_seconds 900, max_attempts 1 and max_parallel_runs 1. The proposal accurately distinguishes this from a general persistent coding DAG.

The Mu worker imports createAgentSession and invokes session.prompt. The host allowlist permits read/write/edit/run_check; run_check accepts a frozen check_id and validates the narrow Go-test argv. The proposal does not claim arbitrary shell or frontend-check capability is already present.

verifyMuTurn explicitly proves finite execution rather than correctness of business repairs. Goal acceptance rejects ordinary non-FIXTURE measurement with 503; LIVE is allowed only for a bound planning Goal, subject to the remaining acceptance checks. The proposal correctly says these paths are not general delivery acceptance and must not be enabled by deleting the guard.

runDispatch preserves an old cancel-cascade branch for no prompt/legacy flags, and NotRoutedWriter refuses writes for the legacy task engine. The proposal identifies their coexistence and includes compatibility/migration risk.

Read the actual RESULT.json and CONTROLLER-TERMINAL.json: C then D completed on 2026-10-28, helper_calls=2, controller outer exit=0, both returned INVALID_REQUEST folder selection cancelled. Both C/cancel.json and D/cancel.json record post_idcancel=false and NO_VISIBLE_OWNED_DIALOG. These are diagnostic completion, not successful selection or native lifecycle acceptance; the proposal correctly supersedes the stale not-started handoff.

Exactly 9 of the 11 scoped source files exist and are untracked in the named worktree. The media test and installation document are absent; the scoped artifact root and builder receipt root do not exist. The proposal correctly avoids calling this active or completed media construction.

design_assessment.retain: Existing Go/SQLite authority, one coordinator per canonical data root, Mu as the bounded worker, shared typed command/event contracts, writer leases/CAS, fixed evidence and recovery semantics.
design_assessment.modify: Canonical per-user host location and authenticated attach, explicit connection/management ownership, public CLI semantics and bounded project iteration/delivery validation.
design_assessment.defer: Additional agent frameworks/state machines/memory stacks and automatic system replacement until existing project-level execution and recovery evidence justify them.
design_assessment.phase_order: The first finite real Go task can be inspected with frozen checks and independent evidence before adding general persistent Goal acceptance; the proposal does not falsely require or claim a general LIVE acceptance implementation in phase 1.
design_assessment.migration_risk: The proposal preserves existing project/database identities, forbids automatic database merging, calls for compatibility mapping of old CLI behavior and versions new Goal capabilities without backfilling old PASS.
design_assessment.permission_boundary: No recommendation lowers current permissions, trusts arbitrary localhost, grants generic shell to renderer/worker, bypasses protected holdout or resets failure counters. The proposed npm/Vite adapter is future scoped work and must remain within the controlled tool boundary already stated by the document.
design_assessment.implementation_preconditions: Concrete protocol, schema, data-root, lifecycle or release-standard changes still need an explicit difference decision and normal scoped review. This document and this review are not such implementation authorization.

review_evidence.final_document_changes: Exactly two announced wording lines changed between the original and final subject; both were independently reviewed.

limits: This is a document fact/architecture recommendation review, not a test of the proposed future behavior.
Existing current fixture/build evidence was inspected/referenced; no tests, Core, Electron product, installer, old-data, holdout or previously blocked native operation was rerun.
The future canonical-path migration, OWNED/ATTACHED management model, typed coding DAG, npm/Vite checks and normal LIVE delivery acceptance remain proposed and unimplemented by this review.
No frozen specification, global checkpoint, acceptance state or failure counter was changed.
